messages.text: The retry change is ready for you. It is forty lines and every one of them is the same idea, so it should not take long.
All five regions are inside the error budget for the first morning in three weeks. Sydney is the quietest of them.
We are getting timeouts out of Sydney, and only Sydney. Nobody here can reproduce it.
Reproduced against the Sydney replica. It is not the region. The retry measures its wait with the wall clock, so anything further away than about 180 ms can retry into its own timeout.
Fix the cause. Not with a bigger timeout.
We have moved you to GPT-6 Sol from today. Same service, same notes.
Understood. The branch and the failing region test are where I left them, so I will carry on.

The retry measures against a clock that only goes forwards, and the region test now covers all five rather than the two we happened to have fixtures for.

Sydney has been clean for eleven hours.

type.text: What was it actually doing before? In plain words.

toolCall.input: git show --stat HEAD && swift test --filter RegionRetryTests
toolCall.output:
3 files changed, 41 insertions(+), 16 deletions(-)
18 tests passed

reply.text:
It timed the wait with the wall clock. When that clock shifted, a two hundred millisecond wait could come back as none at all, so the request fired again straight away and the server saw a burst rather than a retry.

Sydney is far enough away that the burst and the original overlapped. Nearer regions finished before the clock had a chance to move, which is why it only ever happened there.
